title: Auto Loans: application eligibility, funding and the funding window
content:
# Auto Loans: application eligibility, funding and the funding window

This policy of the Auto Loans product category at PCB governs whether an application fits the chosen product, how an approved loan funds, and when an unfunded application is withdrawn. Every product (Used Vehicle, Certified Pre-Owned Vehicle, Auto Refinance, Lease Buyout, New Vehicle and Green Vehicle Loan) applies its own amount range, loan-to-value ceiling, vehicle age and mileage limits, term options, eligible credit grades and APR floor.

## Clauses

1. **Age.** The applicant's age in whole years on the application date, taken from the date of birth on the customer profile, must be at least the product's minimum age. This is judged from the customer profile record, not from the applicant's statement.
2. **Fit to the product.** The amount financed must lie between the product's minimum and maximum amount and be no more than the product's loan-to-value ceiling as a percent of the vehicle value; the vehicle must be no older than the product's vehicle-age limit and have no more than its mileage limit; its powertrain must be one the product accepts; and the term must be one of the product's term options.
3. **Underwriting.** Approval, the credit grade and funding are underwriting decisions made by the credit system. The grade must be one of the product's eligible credit grades.
4. **First due date.** The first due date is no more than the product's latest-first-due-date setting, in calendar days after funding.
5. **Funding.** An approved loan funds by one disbursement of the amount financed, including any GAP charge, paid to the dealer, lessor or prior lender; this creates the principal balance, interest accrues from the funding date, and the loan moves from applied to active as repayment begins.
6. **Funding lapse.** An approved loan not funded is withdrawn once the product's funding window, in calendar days, has passed after the application was recorded. An application also ends as withdrawn when it is declined or withdrawn by the applicant.

## How the funding window is counted

- Clock start: the application date on record.
- Count calendar days with the day after the application date as day 1.
- The application lapses when today is **on or after** the application date plus the window. The boundary day itself counts as lapsed.

## Boundary case (illustrative window, not a product value)

Take an application recorded on 2026-03-02 and, for illustration only, a window of 20 days. Day 1 is 2026-03-03 and day 20 is 2026-03-22.

| Today | Funded yet? | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-03-21 | no | still open; not lapsed |
| 2026-03-22 | no | lapsed: withdrawn |

## Age gate cases (abstract)

| Applicant's birthday that reaches the minimum age | Outcome |
|---|---|
| falls on or before the application date | meets the age gate |
| falls the day after the application date | does not meet the age gate |
